The Kebbi State Government has inaugurated an All Progressives Congress Stakeholders’ Reconciliation Committee to resolve internal disagreements and strengthen the party ahead of forthcoming elections. The committee was inaugurated on Thursday by Governor Nasir Idris, represented by his deputy, Senator Umar Tafida, who charged members to ensure that aggrieved party members were reconciled and the party’s unity restored. The governor urged the committee to discharge its responsibilities with fairness, commitment and a sense of responsibility, stressing that internal cohesion was essential to the party’s electoral success. He said every aggrieved member should be given the opportunity to express their grievances, adding that party leaders must prioritise collective interests over personal differences. According to him, constructive dialogue, mutual understanding and inclusive engagement would help strengthen the party’s structures and improve its chances in forthcoming elections. He said the committee would adopt an inclusive approach by listening to aggrieved members, identifying the causes of disagreements and facilitating lasting solutions. Magoro disclosed that the committee would visit all 21 local government areas of the state to engage party officials, stakeholders and other relevant groups. He said the visits would enable the committee to assess grievances at the grassroots and develop recommendations for strengthening the party. 2027: Alli pledges free education, restoration of Oyo school boards Police arrest 14 over attack on Katsina APC convoy No confusion, Osun will vote Accord candidates, Tinubu for president — Adeleke “Our mission is not merely to settle immediate disputes but also to encourage a culture of dialogue, cooperation and collective responsibility that will sustain party unity beyond the electoral period,” he said. The convener of the committee and Managing Director of the National Airspace Management Agency, Ahmed Faruk Umar, described the initiative as an important platform for addressing legitimate concerns and preventing internal disagreements from undermining the party. He commended Idris for supporting the reconciliation effort and urged party members to cooperate with the committee. Umar called on stakeholders to channel their grievances through constructive engagement, expressing confidence that sustained dialogue would strengthen the APC’s political base. Also speaking, APC chieftain Umar Büro pledged his support for the committee and urged members to “put aside their differences.” He said the success of the exercise would depend on the willingness of party leaders and members to “embrace compromise, mutual respect and collective action.” Similarly, Alhaji Atiku Bunu pledged his support for the initiative, urging stakeholders to avoid actions capable of deepening divisions within the party. The committee is expected to engage stakeholders across the Gwandu, Argungu, Yauri and Zuru Emirates as part of efforts to promote understanding and lasting reconciliation. Retired Justice Sulaiman Ambursa is the vice chairman of the committee, while Rilwanu Abarshi Yauri will serve as secretary. Ahmed Faruk will serve as coordinator. Animashaun Salman
